page.layout: One column of running text, marginal notes in the right margin. Running head top left, page number top right. No catchword, signature or footnotes. A small ornament sits below the last line and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Græci fuerunt dicti. Vulgus tamen Galatas dici vult ἀπὸ τῆς γάλακτος[?], a lacte, quòd homines lacteos hoc est, albos regio illa produceret, quanquam alii cum Diodoro opinantur huic regioni Galatam, filiam Herculis, nomen dedisse.
Trocmi Germani[?] populi a lac[?] ff[?]ndo dicti.] Puta vel à Latina T[?] seu Trucul[?]nti voce; vel ab Germanica, Trotze vel Trutzen, quod est, Minis insolenter lacessere vel provocare.

Tollistobogi a ferendo arcubus cognominati.] Nimirum a Tolleadi verbo Latinorum, & bog vel bogen Germanorum, arcum notante: nisi malis dictos quasi Telistobogos, a telis: vel Balistobogos a balista, voce Latino germanica, ejusdem sensus, quasi populos instructos peritia jaculandi, hoc est, bellicosos. Quo certe tropo jaculans sagittarius dicitur del icosus Ismaël: & Arcu valentes, milites bellicosiores, cum Saule desiderati: & Armati jaculantes arcu, posteri Ephraimi, peritia & rebus militaribus, sive ad defendendum, sive ad laedendum instrumenti.Gen 21,201.Sam.2,24 Psal. 78,9.
main_text.head: GALLI.
main_text.p: Quia Gallorum apud Authores multiplex appellatio est, sub qua continentur non tam CeltoFranci, quàm

page.notes: The two Greek words "ἀπὸ τῆς γάλακτος" are read with doubt, so the last word carries [?]. The line "Trocmi Germani populi a lac ffndo dicti" is badly damaged and is only partly legible. The marginal references are in the right margin next to the lines they belong to; the "24" beside "Psal." may be a stray number and is copied as printed. The running head reads COMMENTARIVS in print and is given here as COMMENTARIUS.
